fullPassage:
You are at a critical stage in your life, trying to figure out who you are and who you want to be. You may also be wondering how you can improve yourself. Self-improvement is not about being perfect. It is a journey to become the best version of yourself. The talks here will inspire you as you take your first steps.

Talk 1 For Those Struggling with Creativity
I'm a writer, and I love writing. But there are moments when I feel anxious about my writing and blame myself for a lack of creativity. Creating something new is not easy, and you have probably experienced this when you had difficulty coming up with ideas for group projects or videos. So, how can we set aside those worries and enjoy the creative process more?

I did some research on this issue and found that ancient Romans understood "genius" differently from how we see it today. To them, "genius" didn't refer to a particularly gifted person but rather a divine assistant spirit of creativity. They believed that geniuses lived in the walls of artists' homes and would come out and help them with their work. This meant that if the artists' work was not good enough, they didn't have to blame themselves entirely. Everyone knew that their genius was also responsible for the quality of the work.

Some people may think this is not scientific, but we often hear stories about how people get inspired mysteriously. I once met an American poet named Ruth Stone. Throughout her life, she worked on a farm and wrote poems. She had a special way of recognizing when a poetic genius was coming to her. She said it felt like the earth was shaking under her feet! Whenever that feeling hit her, she knew she had to return home quickly and write the poem down before the genius found another poet.

My creative process isn't as dramatic as hers. I have to get up at the same time and work on my laptop for hours every day. Yet, even in this rather boring routine, I do get ideas coming from a source I can't identify. Typically, it happens when I'm deeply engaged in my work. Several hours or even days can pass, and I completely immerse myself in my creative process. It's at those moments that a brilliant idea strikes me somewhat mysteriously. I'm sure that's my genius.

Remember that you too have a magical genius that is willing to help you. But first, you must put your heart and soul into your work. Immerse yourself in your work and try to enjoy the creative process itself. If you do, your genius will come for sure.

Talk 2 For Those Worrying about an Uncertain Future
When I was 12, I was passionate about soccer. I played soccer every day, and I always thought that I would grow up to become a great soccer player one day. Forty years later, however, I don't even watch soccer games anymore. I'm actually a big fan of American football now. My 12-year-old self may find this a betrayal.

When I was 22, I graduated from college in India with a computer science degree. At that time, it never occurred to me that I would be living a completely different life in the U.S. as a journalist and podcast host. Thirty years ago, we didn't even have podcasts or smartphones, and the future was not just unknown but unknowable.

When we look back, we can see how we have changed, but when we look forward, we tend to imagine ourselves as the same people, only older and taller. That, however, is not the case. Biologically, our cells are continuously renewing themselves, and our brains are rewiring and modifying their connections. We are constantly becoming new versions of ourselves.

Have you heard of the "Ship of Theseus"? When Theseus, a famous Greek hero, returned from his adventure of rescuing the children of Athens, the Athenians wanted to preserve his ship. They kept replacing the wood pieces that had decayed until all the original pieces were replaced with new ones. In this situation, could we still call it the Ship of Theseus?

Well, we are living examples of the Ship of Theseus. Every day, we are changing and growing to become new versions of ourselves. This means that our future selves may be very different from who we are now. Then how can we create a future we'll be proud of? I have some advice for you.

First, actively envision the kind of person you want to become in the future. To do this, spend time with different kinds of people to learn more and stay curious. Second, when expressing your views online or with friends, remember that your future self might disagree with your current opinions. So, be respectful of other people's opinions and don't just assume that you are always right. Finally, your future self will have strengths and wisdom that you may lack today. Even if you can't do something now, you might be able to in the future. So, don't be afraid of new challenges. Be brave!

questions.passage: You are at a (A)[critical / trivial] stage in your life, trying to figure out who you are and who you want to be. You may also be wondering how you can improve yourself. Self-improvement is not about being perfect. It is a journey to become the best version of yourself. The talks here will (B)[inspire / discourage] you as you take your first steps. But there are moments when I feel (C)[anxious / confident] about my writing and blame myself for a lack of creativity.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 인생의 중요한(critical) 단계에 있으며, 강연이 영감을 줄(inspire) 것이고, 글쓰기에 불안함을 느끼는(anxious) 순간이 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① critical — inspire — anxious: 원문 일치
❌ ② trivial(사소한): critical의 반의어
❌ ③ discourage(낙담시키다): inspire의 반의어
❌ ④ confident(자신감 있는): anxious의 반의어
det.tip: critical(중요한) ↔ trivial(사소한), inspire(영감을 주다) ↔ discourage(낙담시키다), anxious(불안한) ↔ confident(자신감 있는)

questions.passage: I did some research on this issue and found that ancient Romans understood "genius" differently from how we see it today. To them, "genius" didn't refer to a particularly (A)[gifted / ordinary] person but rather a divine assistant spirit of creativity. They believed that geniuses lived in the walls of artists' homes and would come out and help them with their work. This meant that if the artists' work was not good enough, they didn't have to blame themselves (B)[entirely / partially]. Everyone knew that their genius was also (C)[responsible / irrelevant] for the quality of the work.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 특별히 재능 있는(gifted) 사람이 아닌 신성한 영혼을 의미했으며, 자신을 전적으로(entirely) 탓하지 않아도 되었고, genius도 작품 질에 책임이 있었다(responsible).
det.analysis:
✅ ② gifted — entirely — responsible: 원문 일치
❌ ① partially(부분적으로): entirely의 반의어. '전적으로 탓하지 않아도 됐다'가 원문
❌ ③ ordinary(평범한): gifted의 반의어. 'a particularly gifted person'이 원문
❌ ④ irrelevant(무관한): responsible의 반의어. genius도 질에 책임이 있었다는 문맥
det.tip: gifted(재능 있는) ↔ ordinary(평범한), entirely(전적으로) ↔ partially(부분적으로), responsible(책임 있는) ↔ irrelevant(무관한)

questions.passage: When we look back, we can see how we have changed, but when we look forward, we tend to imagine ourselves as the same people, only older and taller. Biologically, our cells are continuously (A)[renewing / deteriorating] themselves, and our brains are rewiring and (B)[modifying / preserving] their connections. We are constantly becoming new versions of ourselves. First, actively (C)[envision / ignore] the kind of person you want to become in the future.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 세포는 계속 스스로를 새것으로 바꾸고(renewing), 뇌는 연결을 수정하고(modifying) 있다. 미래에 되고 싶은 사람을 적극적으로 마음속에 그려라(envision).
det.analysis:
✅ ③ renewing — modifying — envision: 원문 일치
❌ ① preserving(보존하는): modifying의 반의어. 뇌가 연결을 수정한다는 문맥
❌ ② deteriorating(악화되는): renewing의 반의어. 새로운 버전이 된다는 긍정적 맥락
❌ ④ ignore(무시하다): envision의 반의어. 조언으로서 미래를 그려보라는 맥락
det.tip: renewing(새롭게 하는) ↔ deteriorating(악화되는), modifying(수정하는) ↔ preserving(보존하는), envision(마음속에 그리다) ↔ ignore(무시하다)

questions.passage: Creating something new is not easy, and you have probably ①<u>experienced</u> this when you had difficulty coming up with ideas for group projects or videos. So, how can we set aside those ②<u>worries</u> and enjoy the creative process more? Remember that you too have a magical genius that is ③<u>willing</u> to help you. But first, you must put your heart and soul into your work. ④<u>Neglect</u> yourself in your work and try to enjoy the creative process itself.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문은 '몰입하라(Immerse)'인데, '방치하라(Neglect)'로 바뀌었다. 일에 심혈을 기울이고 몰입하라는 조언이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① experienced(경험했다): 원문 일치
✅ ② worries(걱정들): 원문 일치
✅ ③ willing(기꺼이 하는): 원문 일치
❌ ④ Neglect(방치하다) → Immerse(몰입하다): 반의어로 교체됨
det.tip: immerse(몰입하다) ↔ neglect(방치하다). 'put your heart and soul(심혈을 기울이다)' 뒤에 같은 맥락으로 '몰입하라'가 와야 자연스럽다.

questions.passage: When I was 12, I was ①<u>passionate</u> about soccer. I played soccer every day, and I always thought that I would grow up to become a great soccer player one day. When I was 22, I graduated from college in India with a computer science degree. At that time, it never ②<u>occurred</u> to me that I would be living a completely different life in the U.S. as a journalist and podcast host. When we look back, we can see how we have changed, but when we look forward, we tend to ③<u>imagine</u> ourselves as the same people, only older and taller. They kept replacing the wood pieces that had ④<u>flourished</u> until all the original pieces were replaced with new ones.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① 원문은 '썩은(decayed)'인데, '번성한(flourished)'으로 바뀌었다. 나무 조각이 썩어서 교체했다는 맥락이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ④ flourished(번성한) → decayed(썩은): 반의어로 교체됨. 교체 이유가 썩어서이므로 flourished는 맥락에 안 맞음
✅ ② occurred(생각났다): 'it never occurred to me' 원문 일치
✅ ③ imagine(상상하다): 원문 일치
✅ ① passionate(열정적인): 원문 일치
det.tip: decayed(썩은, 부패한) ↔ flourished(번성한). 배를 보존하기 위해 '썩은' 나무를 교체했다는 문맥.

questions.passage: I once met an American poet named Ruth Stone. Throughout her life, she worked on a farm and wrote poems. She had a ①<u>special</u> way of recognizing when a poetic genius was coming to her. She said it felt like the earth was shaking under her feet! Whenever that feeling hit her, she knew she had to return home quickly and write the poem down before the genius found another poet. My creative process isn't as ②<u>dramatic</u> as hers. Yet, even in this rather boring routine, I do get ideas coming from a source I can't ③<u>identify</u>. Typically, it happens when I'm deeply ④<u>detached</u> in my work.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문은 '몰두하고 있는(engaged)'인데, '분리된(detached)'으로 바뀌었다. 작업에 깊이 몰두할 때 아이디어가 떠오른다는 문맥이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① special(특별한): 원문 일치
✅ ② dramatic(극적인): 원문 일치
✅ ③ identify(확인하다, 파악하다): 원문 일치
❌ ④ detached(분리된, 초연한) → engaged(몰두한): 반의어로 교체됨. 뒤에 '완전히 몰입한다(immerse)'가 나오므로 detached는 모순
det.tip: engaged(몰두한) ↔ detached(초연한, 무관심한). deeply engaged = 깊이 빠져있는. 이후 'immerse myself'도 같은 의미.

questions.passage: You are at a critical stage in your life, trying to figure out who you are and who you want to be. You may also be wondering how you can improve yourself. Self-improvement is not about being perfect. It is a __________ to become the best version of yourself. The talks here will inspire you as you take your first steps.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 자기 계발은 완벽해짐이 아니라 최고의 버전이 되기 위한 여정(journey)이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② journey(여정): 원문 일치. 과정과 성장을 강조하는 맥락
❌ ① destination(목적지): 도착점이 아닌 과정을 말하는 문맥과 맞지 않음
❌ ③ obstacle(장애물): 부정적 의미로 문맥과 불일치
❌ ④ competition(경쟁): 자기 계발과 경쟁은 다른 맥락
det.tip: journey(여정): 목적지가 아닌 과정 자체를 강조할 때 쓰는 표현. 'life is a journey, not a destination'과 같은 맥락.

questions.passage: I did some research on this issue and found that ancient Romans understood "genius" differently from how we see it today. To them, "genius" didn't refer to a particularly gifted person but rather a divine assistant spirit of creativity. They believed that geniuses lived in the walls of artists' homes and would come out and help them with their work. This meant that if the artists' work was not good enough, they didn't have to __________ themselves entirely.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 예술가의 작품이 충분하지 못해도 자기 자신을 전적으로 탓하지(blame) 않아도 되었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ blame(탓하다): 원문 일치. genius도 책임이 있었으므로
❌ ① praise(칭찬하다): 작품이 좋지 않은 상황이므로 칭찬은 맥락에 안 맞음
❌ ② express(표현하다): 문맥상 자책의 의미가 필요
❌ ④ reward(보상하다): 작품 실패 맥락에 안 맞음
det.tip: blame oneself(자책하다) = 자기 자신을 탓하다. 고대 로마인들은 genius 덕분에 전적으로 자책하지 않아도 되었다.

questions.passage: When we look back, we can see how we have changed, but when we look forward, we tend to imagine ourselves as the same people, only older and taller. That, however, is not the case. Biologically, our cells are continuously renewing themselves, and our brains are rewiring and modifying their connections. We are constantly becoming new versions of ourselves. Well, we are living examples of the Ship of Theseus. This means that our future selves may be very different from who we are now. Then how can we create a future we'll be __________?
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 미래의 우리는 지금과 매우 다를 수 있다. 그렇다면 우리가 자랑스러워할(proud of) 미래를 어떻게 만들 수 있을까?
det.analysis:
✅ ④ proud of(자랑스러워하는): 원문 일치. 긍정적 미래 설계를 권유
❌ ① ashamed of(부끄러워하는): 반의어. 긍정적 조언 맥락
❌ ② indifferent to(무관심한): 미래에 무관심하라는 맥락 아님
❌ ③ worried about(걱정하는): Talk 2 제목이 '불확실한 미래를 걱정하는 이들을 위해'이므로 걱정에서 벗어나라는 취지
det.tip: be proud of(~을 자랑스러워하다). 이 글의 핵심 메시지: 불확실한 미래를 두려워하지 말고, 자랑스러운 미래를 만들어라.

questions.passage: She had a special way of <u>recognizing</u> when a poetic genius was coming to her. She said it felt like the earth was shaking under her feet! Whenever that feeling hit her, she knew she had to return home quickly and write the poem down before the genius found another poet.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>recognizing</u>과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 시적 천재가 다가오는 때를 알아차리는(recognizing) 특별한 방법이 있었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① identifying(알아보는, 파악하는): recognizing의 동의어
❌ ② ignoring(무시하는): recognizing의 반의어
❌ ③ creating(만드는): 전혀 다른 의미
❌ ④ forgetting(잊는): 기억/인지와 반대
det.tip: recognize = identify = 알아보다, 인식하다. 두 단어 모두 '무언가를 파악하다'의 의미.

questions.passage: Biologically, our cells are continuously renewing themselves, and our brains are rewiring and modifying their connections. We are constantly becoming new versions of ourselves. Have you heard of the "Ship of Theseus"? When Theseus, a famous Greek hero, returned from his adventure of rescuing the children of Athens, the Athenians wanted to <u>preserve</u> his ship.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>preserve</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 아테네인들은 테세우스의 배를 보존하고(preserve) 싶어 했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ maintain(유지하다): preserve의 동의어. 원래 상태를 지키다
❌ ① destroy(파괴하다): preserve의 반의어
❌ ② abandon(포기하다): 보존과 반대
❌ ④ rebuild(재건하다): 유사해 보이지만, 보존은 현 상태 유지이고 재건은 새로 만드는 것
det.tip: preserve = maintain = keep = 보존하다, 유지하다. preserve는 '원래 상태를 지키다'에 초점.

questions.passage: Several hours or even days can pass, and I completely <u>immerse</u> myself in my creative process. It's at those moments that a brilliant idea strikes me somewhat mysteriously. I'm sure that's my genius. Remember that you too have a magical genius that is willing to help you.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>immerse</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 창작 과정에 완전히 몰입한다(immerse).
det.analysis:
✅ ② absorb(몰두시키다): immerse의 동의어. absorb oneself = immerse oneself
❌ ① withdraw(물러나다): 몰입의 반대
❌ ③ distract(산만하게 하다): 집중의 반대
❌ ④ isolate(고립시키다): 물리적 분리이지 정신적 몰입이 아님
det.tip: immerse = absorb = engross = 몰두하다. 'immerse oneself in' = 'be absorbed in' = ~에 빠져들다.

questions.passage: When I was 22, I graduated from college in India with a computer science degree. At that time, it never occurred to me that I would be living a completely different life in the U.S. as a journalist and podcast host. Thirty years ago, we didn't even have podcasts or smartphones, and the future was not just unknown but <u>unknowable</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>unknowable</u>과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 미래는 단지 알려지지 않은 것이 아니라 알 수 없는(unknowable) 것이었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ predictable(예측 가능한): unknowable의 반의어. 알 수 없는 ↔ 예측 가능한
❌ ① invisible(보이지 않는): 시각적 의미로 다른 범주
❌ ② uncertain(불확실한): unknowable과 유사한 의미(동의어에 가까움)
❌ ③ mysterious(신비로운): unknowable과 유사한 뉘앙스
det.tip: unknowable(알 수 없는) ↔ predictable(예측 가능한). un- 접두사 = 부정. knowable = 알 수 있는.

questions.passage: Second, when expressing your views online or with friends, remember that your future self might disagree with your current opinions. So, be <u>respectful</u> of other people's opinions and don't just assume that you are always right.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>respectful</u>과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 다른 사람들의 의견을 존중하는(respectful) 태도를 가져라.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ dismissive(무시하는, 경멸하는): respectful의 반의어. 존중하는 ↔ 무시하는
❌ ① careful(조심스러운): 유사한 긍정적 태도
❌ ② polite(공손한): respectful의 유의어
❌ ④ humble(겸손한): 역시 긍정적 태도로 반의어가 아님
det.tip: respectful(존중하는) ↔ dismissive(무시하는). dismissive는 '무시하는, 경시하는'으로 타인의 의견을 하찮게 여기는 태도.

questions.passage:
(A) It's at those moments that a brilliant idea <u>strikes</u> me somewhat mysteriously.
(B) When I was 12, I was passionate about soccer. I played soccer every day. The ball <u>strikes</u> the goalpost and bounces back.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 (A)와 (B)의 strikes가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 기발한 아이디어가 다소 신비롭게 떠오른다(strikes). (B) 공이 골대를 때린다(strikes).
det.analysis:
✅ ② (A) 떠오르다 — (B) 때리다: (A)는 '생각이 갑자기 떠오르다', (B)는 물리적 충돌
❌ ① 의미 뒤바뀜
❌ ③ 공격하다: (A)의 맥락에서 아이디어가 '공격한다'는 부자연스러움
❌ ④ 파업하다: (B)는 축구 맥락이므로 파업이 아님
det.tip: strike의 다의어: ① (생각이) 떠오르다 (An idea strikes me) ② 때리다/치다 (strike the ball) ③ 파업하다 (go on strike). 문맥에 따라 의미가 완전히 달라진다.

questions.stem:
다음 영영 풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?
"to form a mental image of something, especially something that may happen in the future"

det.korean: 특히 미래에 일어날 수 있는 것에 대해 머릿속에 이미지를 형성하다 = envision(마음속에 그리다)
det.analysis:
✅ ① envision(마음속에 그리다): 영영 풀이와 정확히 일치
❌ ② examine(조사하다): 이미지 형성이 아닌 분석/검사
❌ ③ encounter(마주치다): 우연히 만나다
❌ ④ enhance(향상시키다): 개선의 의미
det.tip: envision = visualize = imagine = 마음속에 그리다. en-(안에) + vision(시각) = 마음의 눈으로 보다.

questions.passage: Creating something new is not easy, and you have probably experienced this when you had difficulty coming up with ideas. She had a special way of recognizing when a poetic genius was coming to her. My __________ (create) process isn't as dramatic as hers.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 나의 창작(creative) 과정은 그녀의 것만큼 극적이지 않다.
det.analysis: create(동사) → creative(형용사): process(명사)를 수식하므로 형용사형 필요
det.tip: create(동사, 만들다) → creative(형용사, 창의적인) → creativity(명사, 창의성) → creation(명사, 창작물)

questions.passage: Biologically, our cells are continuously renewing themselves, and our brains are rewiring and modifying their connections. We are __________ (constant) becoming new versions of ourselves.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 우리는 끊임없이(constantly) 새로운 버전의 우리 자신이 되고 있다.
det.analysis: constant(형용사) → constantly(부사): 동사 becoming을 수식하므로 부사형 필요
det.tip: constant(형용사, 끊임없는) → constantly(부사, 끊임없이). -ly를 붙여 부사로 전환.

questions.passage: Some people may think this is not scientific, but we often hear stories about how people get inspired mysteriously. I once met an American poet named Ruth Stone. Throughout her life, she worked on a farm and wrote poems. She said it felt like the earth was shaking under her feet! Whenever that feeling hit her, she knew she had to return home quickly and write the poem down before the genius __________.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: genius가 다른 시인을 찾기(found another poet) 전에 빨리 집으로 돌아가 시를 적어야 했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② found another poet(다른 시인을 찾았다): 원문 일치
❌ ① helped her finish: genius가 떠나기 전에 잡아야 한다는 맥락과 맞지 않음
❌ ③ disappeared from the farm: 농장에서 사라진다는 내용 없음
❌ ④ returned to the wall: 벽은 로마인의 genius 이야기이지 Ruth Stone의 이야기가 아님
det.tip: Ruth Stone의 genius는 그녀에게 다가왔다가 다른 시인에게 갈 수 있었으므로 빨리 적어야 했다.

questions.passage: When we look back, we can see how we have changed, but when we look forward, we tend to imagine ourselves as the same people, only older and taller. That, however, is not the case. Have you heard of the "Ship of Theseus"? They kept replacing the wood pieces that had decayed until all the original pieces were replaced with new ones. Well, we are living examples of the Ship of Theseus. Every day, we are changing and growing to become new versions of ourselves. This means that __________.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: we should try to stay the same person throughout our lives
our future selves may be very different from who we are now
the ship can never truly be called the Ship of Theseus
looking forward is more reliable than looking backward

det.korean: 이는 곧 미래의 우리 모습이 지금의 우리 모습과 매우 다를 수 있음을 의미한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① our future selves may be very different from who we are now: 원문 일치
❌ ② 같은 사람으로 남아야 한다: 글의 핵심(계속 변화한다)과 정반대
❌ ③ 배를 테세우스의 배라 부를 수 없다: 이건 질문이었지 결론이 아님
❌ ④ 앞을 보는 게 더 신뢰할 만하다: 본문은 앞을 볼 때 변화를 과소평가한다고 말함
det.tip: 테세우스의 배 비유: 우리 몸의 세포가 계속 바뀌듯, 미래의 자신은 현재와 매우 다를 수 있다는 메시지.
